text: Acute coronary syndrome includes unstable angina and myocardial infarction caused by acute coronary ischemia. Initial assessment includes symptoms, electrocardiography, and cardiac troponin testing. Persistent ST-segment elevation suggests an occlusive myocardial infarction pathway requiring urgent reperfusion assessment.

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease causes persistent respiratory symptoms and airflow limitation. Diagnosis requires compatible clinical features and spirometry demonstrating persistent airflow obstruction after appropriate bronchodilator assessment. Exacerbations may present with worsening dyspnea, cough, and sputum.

Hyperkalemia refers to an abnormally elevated serum potassium concentration. Severe hyperkalemia can produce muscle weakness and dangerous cardiac conduction abnormalities. Management depends on severity, electrocardiographic findings, and the underlying cause.

Bacterial meningitis is an acute infection of the meninges that can cause fever, headache, neck stiffness, altered mental status, and other neurologic findings. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis and microbiologic testing support diagnosis when clinically appropriate, while treatment should not be unnecessarily delayed in a critically ill patient.

Diabetic ketoacidosis is characterized by hyperglycemia or diabetes-range glucose with ketosis and metabolic acidosis. Common manifestations include polyuria, polydipsia, vomiting, abdominal pain, dehydration, and altered consciousness. Management requires fluid replacement, insulin, and careful electrolyte monitoring.

Acute ischemic stroke presents with sudden focal neurologic deficits caused by cerebral ischemia. Rapid assessment of symptom onset or last-known-well time and brain imaging is essential. Eligible patients may require intravenous thrombolysis or endovascular thrombectomy depending on clinical and imaging criteria.

Acute kidney injury is an abrupt reduction in kidney function reflected by a rise in serum creatinine, reduced urine output, or both. Evaluation should review volume status, nephrotoxic exposures, obstruction, and other reversible causes. Management focuses on treating the cause and avoiding additional kidney injury.

Community-acquired pneumonia is an acute infection of the lung parenchyma that commonly causes cough, fever, sputum production, and dyspnea. Diagnosis integrates clinical assessment with chest imaging when indicated. Severity assessment helps determine outpatient versus inpatient management.
